/.visibleText: AI assurance for public institutions Clear, accountable decisions about AI use MIZAN brings together evidence, expert review and human approval for a specific AI use. It records who approved it, what the AI may do, the conditions attached, and when the decision needs review. AI assurance means checking and documenting whether an AI use is fit for its purpose and its operating conditions. Discuss a pilot View the approval record In development. Exploring a focused design-partner pilot. Illustrative concept using sample information. It does not represent a live deployment or final product interface. Approval record snapshot AI use Resident service assistant (constructed) Purpose Explain published requirements and route complex cases to staff. Accountable owner Service delivery director Decision Authorised, with conditions Review date 30 January 2027 Watch MIZAN A short introduction to accountable AI approval See how MIZAN frames evidence, authority and human responsibility around a specific AI use. شاهد ميزان مقدمة قصيرة عن الموافقة المسؤولة على استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي تعرّف على كيفية ربط ميزان بين الأدلة والصلاحية والمسؤولية البشرية حول استخدام محدد للذكاء الاصطناعي. Approval record What an accountable AI approval record contains The approval record is the maintained artifact. It separates what the AI may do, what remains a human decision, which evidence was reviewed, and when the approval needs review. Illustrative concept using sample information. It does not represent a live deployment or final product interface. Resident service assistant approval AI use Resident-facing assistant for a public service. Purpose Explain published requirements, help residents prepare information, and route complex cases. Accountable owner Service delivery director. Allowed Use approved guidance, draft explanations, route cases to staff. Not allowed Make eligibility decisions, change records, or send final notices. Evidence Service policy, privacy and security review, accessibility testing, answer-quality review. Decision Authorised, with conditions Conditions Staff review for ambiguous cases; complaint signals trigger review. Review date 30 January 2027. Benefits Why institutions use an approval record P Make responsibility clear. Name the person responsible for the approval and the people who review the evidence. D Keep the basis for approval together. Link the decision to the assessments, policies and conditions that support it. C Know when to review. Flag changes that may affect the approval and route them for human review. The problem AI approval depends on more than a technical test An AI system may perform well while important questions remain unanswered: who can approve its use, can the organisation supervise it, what must stay a human decision, and what happens if the system or its purpose changes. Evidence spread across teams. Policies, tests and reviews often sit in different documents and systems. Unclear basis for approval. A decision may be recorded without a clear link to its evidence, limits and owner. Changes after launch. A new model, policy, permission or incident may require the original decision to be reviewed. People and public purpose Keep people in control of consequential decisions Public service AI should stay understandable, accessible and open to challenge. The approval record should define when staff must intervene, what decisions remain with people, and how concerns reach the responsible team. Credibility and development Applied research connected to practical delivery MIZAN is being developed through Arrownex's AI for Public Purpose Lab in the UAE. The work combines institutional governance, privacy and public policy expertise with engineering and security delivery. The methodology draws on public sector guidance and research on accountability, institutional capability and AI assurance. Pilot work will test whether the approach produces clearer decisions, reuses existing evidence and identifies when review is needed. Arrownex Delivery. AI for Public Purpose Lab Method. UCL IIPP Doctoral research, individual affiliation. FAQ Quick answers before you get in touch What does MIZAN do? MIZAN records the evidence, conditions, owner, approval decision and review date for a specific institutional AI use. Who makes the approval decision? The institution does. MIZAN is designed to make the decision basis clear and reviewable. Does MIZAN produce a score? No. The decision is recorded in words, not a score. Can we use it today? MIZAN is in development and exploring focused design-partner pilots. A pilot would start with one clearly defined AI use. Build the first case around your institution Start with one AI use, one accountable owner and an agreed operating environment. Together, we can map the evidence, define the conditions for approval and agree how the pilot's value will be measured. What we would agree: scope and responsibilities; evidence and review requirements; pilot deliverables and acceptance criteria. Discuss a pilot

/about/.title: About | MIZAN
/about/.description: About Arrownex, the AI for Public Purpose Lab and the named leadership behind MIZAN.
/about/.visibleText: About Connecting AI delivery with institutional responsibility MIZAN is being developed through Arrownex's AI for Public Purpose Lab in the UAE. The Lab brings applied research and institutional assurance into practical AI delivery for government and regulated organisations. People Named leadership behind MIZAN TM Tariq Makadi Co-founder and institutional governance lead. Brings experience in privacy, AI governance and digital public infrastructure to MIZAN's design. As a doctoral researcher at UCL's Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose, he researches the relationship between digital infrastructure, institutions and legitimacy. SK Sujit Kumar Co-founder and Arrownex delivery lead. Leads Arrownex's technology delivery, partnerships and customer relationships, connecting the venture to engineering and operational capability. Operating relationships Arrownex, the Lab and institutional responsibility Arrownex provides the operating and delivery platform. The AI for Public Purpose Lab develops and tests the methods and product proposition. The institution using MIZAN keeps responsibility for its AI approval decisions.

Four instruments Secondary tools, not a competing front door Qudra Institutional capability. Examines institutional capability for this specific use. Explore capability Mu'tamad Human competence. Defines and assesses the knowledge and skills required of named reviewers and supervisors. Explore accountable roles Isnad Evidence and knowledge provenance. Records where knowledge and evidence came from, who reviewed it, and when it needs updating. Explore evidence sources Misbar Controlled research. /how-it-works/.title: How It Works | MIZAN
/how-it-works/.description: How MIZAN supports evidence-backed AI approval decisions.
/how-it-works/.visibleText: How it works How MIZAN works MIZAN helps your team define the AI use, check the evidence, approve it, and review it when things change. Six clear steps From definition to review Define Set the AI use, decision boundary and responsible owner at a high level. Evidence Bring relevant existing evidence into view for the approval discussion. Assess Review whether the available evidence supports the proposed use. Authorise Record the human decision, conditions and review date. Monitor Keep the approval visible as the use and operating context change. Reauthorise Material changes trigger a review before the approval is continued or changed. Change If the AI use changes, review the approval Material changes trigger a review before the AI use moves beyond its approved scope. What can happen? The approval can continue, be limited, be paused, or be stopped. MIZAN records the reason and review date in plain words.

/platform/.title: Platform | MIZAN
/platform/.description: One record for evidence, approval and review of institutional AI use.
/platform/.visibleText: Platform One record for evidence, approval and review MIZAN is being developed to help institutions connect an AI use to the evidence, people and conditions that support its approval. The record is designed to stay reviewable as the system and its operating environment change. Discuss your requirements Illustrative public examples are available for discussion, not as live deployments. Approval record The maintained record keeps the AI use, accountable owner, decision, conditions and review date visible. View the sample approval record Core capabilities What the platform helps you check and record Define the approval. Record the purpose, responsible owner, permitted actions, limits and review date. Connect the evidence. Bring relevant policies, assessments and technical reports into the approval record. Record specialist review. Keep specialist findings and required conditions visible to the decision owner. Check organisational capability. Consider institutional capability for this specific use. Review changes. Material changes trigger a review. Recover the history. Show what was known, what was reviewed, who decided, and the conditions attached. Working with existing systems Designed to use the evidence institutions already hold MIZAN is designed to use evidence from existing risk, privacy, security and AI evaluation processes. Deployment requirements should be agreed privately for each pilot. Positioning Governance tools ask whether the system is safe. MIZAN asks whether the institution is entitled to let it act.
